title: The creative-platform purge wave - activist -> payment-processor pressure on art/game storefronts (Collective Shout, Steam, itch.io, Clip Studio)
source: Public record: Collective Shout (Australian anti-porn group) open letter (Jul 2025) to PayPal/Visa/Mastercard demanding they cut platforms hosting NSFW games (trigger title 'No Mercy'); Steam removed hundreds of adult titles ~a week later citing 'rules and standards set forth by our payment processors and their related card networks and banks' (Valve); itch.io de-indexed all adult NSFW content 31 Jul 2025 citing 'scrutiny from our payment processors' (later began re-indexing free content); processor statements (Stripe 'we do not support adult content'; Mastercard 'has not evaluated any game'; PayPal 'violates ... policies of our partner banks and card networks'); CBC Day6 + Aftermath + itch.io devlogs coverage. PLUS: Clip Studio Assets / CELSYS mass 'set to private' of creator materials + a 23 Sep 2026 apology announcing a move to age restrictions / regional controls / user preferences (self-stated as moderation for a mixed-age global audience; CELSYS did NOT cite payment processors). Overlay on the Financial_Censorship + age-verification + speech-regulation threads (structural; no financial-core edges). HONESTY: takedowns/dates/quotes = FACT; the activist->processor CAUSAL chain is strongly evidenced for Steam/itch (platforms said so) but the processors deny being 'swayed' - so motive/coordination is CONTESTED; the CSP tie is 'same wave' but CELSYS's stated reason is age/regional moderation, NOT payment pressure - labeled interpretation, not asserted.

edges.notes: Collective Shout (Melbourne-based anti-porn/anti-exploitation group) published a Jul 2025 open letter to PayPal/Visa/Mastercard demanding they stop processing for platforms hosting NSFW games (citing 'rape, incest and child sexual abuse' content, trigger title 'No Mercy'). The activist->processor pressure channel - the same shape as NCOSE (fact of the campaign; whether it 'swayed' the networks is denied by them = contested).

Collective Shout is the Australian analogue of NCOSE - allied anti-exploitation activist groups that use the card-network/processor pressure channel to force adult-content takedowns (peer relationship; fact of the shared tactic).

Collective Shout is an activist input to the financial-censorship mechanism: pressure aimed at the payment layer rather than at courts or legislatures - private de-monetization of legal (if offensive) content (fact of the mechanism; child-protection vs morality-driven-speech-suppression framing contested).

Steam (Valve, ~132m MAU) removed hundreds of adult titles ~a week after the open letter, stating some games 'may violate the rules and standards set forth by our payment processors and their related card networks and banks' and that 'loss of payment methods would prevent customers from ... purchas[ing] other titles' - the platform ITSELF named payment processors as the cause (fact; a clear case of the money-rail gating a legal storefront).

itch.io de-indexed ALL adult NSFW content from browse/search on 31 Jul 2025, saying it 'came under scrutiny from our payment processors' and had to 'prioritize our relationship with our payment partners' - later began RE-INDEXING free adult content + slowly reintroducing paid, after mass user call-in campaigns (fact; also an honest counter-example - some of it was reversible, like OnlyFans).
Steam + itch.io were the direct targets of Collective Shout's campaign (fact of the targeting).

Clip Studio Assets (CELSYS, the Clip Studio Paint marketplace) apologized on 23 Sep 2026 for mass-'privating' creator materials and announced a move to 'strengthen the system to include age restrictions, regional controls, and user preferences' so materials publish 'to the appropriate audiences' - i.e. building age/geo-gating into an art-asset store (fact of the announcement; CELSYS cited a mixed-age global audience, NOT payment processors).

CSP's 2026 move fits the SAME wave as the Steam/itch purge and the UK/EU/AU age regimes - creative platforms pre-emptively moderating + age/region-gating expression to stay 'universally accessible' and compliant. The join to payment-processor pressure specifically is INTERPRETATION (CELSYS did not state it); the join to the broader age-verification/speech-regulation climate is well-supported (labeled).

The purge wave sits at the intersection of the financial chokepoint and the speech-regulation climate - itch/Steam actions were processor-driven, but occurred amid the UK OSA / AU eSafety / EU push that raised platform legal exposure for adult content generally (interpretation of the joint pressure; fact that both pressures were live in 2025-26).
